title_en: Fragments of a Prayer and Exorcism
author: Epiphanius of Salamis
occasion: The text is a liturgical fragment for invoking God and commanding an unclean spirit to depart, preserved under the name of Epiphanius of Salamis.
argument: The speaker calls upon God the Almighty, the Lord Jesus Christ, the heavenly king, and upon the maker of heaven and earth. The speaker then adjures an unclean spirit by the word of God, namely the one who made heaven and earth. The spirit is told to fear the one who is clothed with light as with a garment, the one alone having immortality and unapproachable light. The fragment closes with a doxology ascribing glory and dominion to God forever.

outline.move: The same prayer-exorcism text appears in all four sections, which are editorial divisions or multiple witnesses of a single fragment rather than authorial repetitions: invocation of God, adjuration of the unclean spirit, call to fear the God of light, and closing doxology.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The speaker calls upon God the Almighty, the Lord Jesus Christ, the heavenly king, and upon the maker of heaven and earth.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἐπικαλούμεθά σε, Θεὲ παντοκράτορ Κύριε Ἰησοῦ Χριστὲ οὐράνιε βασιλεῦ· ἐπικούμεθά σε τὸν ποιήσαντα τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν
_unresolved_facts.fix: The speaker calls upon God the Almighty, the Lord Jesus Christ, the heavenly king, who is the maker of heaven and earth (second person singular, not 'upon' as a separate entity).

_unresolved_facts.claim: The speaker then adjures an unclean spirit by the word of God, namely the one who made heaven and earth.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἐξορκίζω σε, πνεῦμα ἀκάθαρτον, κατὰ τοῦ λόγου Θεοῦ τοῦ ποιήσαντος τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν
_unresolved_facts.fix: The speaker adjures the unclean spirit by the word of God who made heaven and earth (the relative clause modifies 'word of God', not a separate 'namely' apposition; 'λόγου Θεοῦ' is 'word of God' or 'Logos of God').

_unresolved_facts.claim: The spirit is told to fear the one who is clothed with light as with a garment
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: φοβήθητι τὸν ἀναβαλλόμενον φῶς ὡς ἱμάτιον
_unresolved_facts.fix: The spirit is told to fear the one who puts on/wraps himself with light as with a garment (ἀναβαλλόμενον is middle voice, 'puts on for himself', not passive 'is clothed').

_unresolved_facts.claim: The almighty God, addressed as Lord Jesus Christ and heavenly king.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Θεὲ παντοκράτορ Κύριε Ἰησοῦ Χριστὲ οὐράνιε βασιλεῦ
_unresolved_facts.fix: The almighty God, identified as Lord Jesus Christ and heavenly king (the vocatives are in apposition to a single addressee, not separate entities; this is a Christological identification of Jesus as God Almighty).

_unresolved_facts.claim: First-person plural invocation and first-person singular exorcism
_unresolved_facts.fix: The brief correctly notes the grammatical shift but should clarify: the plural ἐπικαλούμεθά suggests communal/liturgical prayer, while the singular ἐξορκίζω suggests individual exorcist authority, a significant liturgical feature.
